sanskrit: kṣaṇena tad vanaṃ caiva te caivāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ gandharvāḥ pādapāś caiva sarvam antaradhīyata
english: In an instant that forest, and the throngs of Apsarases, and the Gandharvas, and the trees as well—all of it vanished away.

sanskrit: niḥśabdam abhavac cāpi gaṅgākūlaṃ punar nṛpa kuśavalmīkabhūyiṣṭhaṃ babhūva ca yathā purā
english: The bank of the Gaṅgā fell silent once more, O king, and became thick with kuśa-grass and anthills, just as it had been before.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā kuśikaḥ sabhāryas tena karmaṇā vismayaṃ paramaṃ prāptas tad dṛṣṭvā mahad adbhutam
english: Then king Kuśika, together with his wife, beholding that great marvel, was struck by that deed with the utmost astonishment.

sanskrit: tataḥ provāca kuśiko bhāryāṃ harṣasamanvitaḥ paśya bhadre yathā bhāvāś citrā dṛṣṭāḥ sudurlabhāḥ
english: Then Kuśika, filled with delight, said to his wife: "Behold, good lady, what wondrous, exceedingly rare splendors we have seen!

sanskrit: prasādād bhṛgumukhyasya kim anyatra tapobalāt tapasā tad avāpyaṃ hi yan na śakyaṃ manorathaiḥ
english: By the grace of the foremost of the Bhṛgus—whence else but from the power of austerity? For by austerity is attained that which cannot be won by mere wishing.

sanskrit: trailokyarājyād api hi tapa eva viśiṣyate tapasā hi sutaptena krīḍaty eṣa tapodhanaḥ
english: Austerity surpasses even the sovereignty of the three worlds; for through austerity well practiced this man, whose wealth is austerity, sports as he pleases.

sanskrit: aho prabhāvo brahmarṣeś cyavanasya mahātmanaḥ icchann eṣa tapovīryād anyāṃl lokān sṛjed api
english: Ah, the might of the great-souled Brahmā-sage Cyavana! Should he so wish, by the force of his austerity he could even create other worlds.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā eva jāyeran puṇyavāgbuddhikarmaṇaḥ utsahed iha kartuṃ hi ko 'nyo vai cyavanād ṛte
english: Brāhmaṇas alone would be born—holy in speech, in thought, and in deed; for who else but Cyavana could here have the power to do such a thing?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇyaṃ durlabhaṃ loke rājyaṃ hi sulabhaṃ naraiḥ brāhmaṇyasya prabhāvād dhi rathe yuktau svadhuryavat
english: Brāhmaṇhood is hard to attain in this world, while sovereignty is easily gained by men; for through the power of his Brāhmaṇhood we two were yoked to his chariot like well-matched draught-horses.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ cintayānaḥ sa viditaś cyavanasya vai saṃprekṣyovāca sa nṛpaṃ kṣipram āgamyatām iti
english: As the king mused thus, he became known to Cyavana, who, looking upon him, said to him: "Come hither at once."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sahabhāryas tam abhyagacchan mahāmunim śirasā vandanīyaṃ tam avandata sa pārthivaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the king together with his wife approached the great sage, and bowed with his head to that one worthy of reverence.

sanskrit: tasyāśiṣaḥ prayujyātha sa munis taṃ narādhipam niṣīdety abravīd dhīmān sāntvayan puruṣarṣabha
english: Then the wise sage, having pronounced his blessings upon the lord of men, said to him, "Be seated," speaking gently to him, O bull among men.

sanskrit: tataḥ prakṛtim āpanno bhārgavo nṛpate nṛpam uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā tarpayann iva bhārata
english: Then the descendant of Bhṛgu, returned to his natural calm, O king, addressed the monarch in smooth speech, as if refreshing him, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: rājan samyag jitānīha pañca pañcasu yat tvayā manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi kṛcchrān mukto 'si tena vai
english: "O king, since you have here rightly conquered the five senses among the five objects, with the mind as the sixth, by that very feat you are released from peril.

sanskrit: samyag ārādhitaḥ putra tvayāhaṃ vadatāṃ vara na hi te vṛjinaṃ kiṃ cit susūkṣmam api vidyate
english: You have rightly propitiated me, my son, O best of speakers; not the slightest fault, however subtle, is found in you.

sanskrit: anujānīhi māṃ rājan gamiṣyāmi yathāgatam prīto 'smi tava rājendra varaś ca pratigṛhyatām
english: Give me leave, O king; I shall depart as I came. I am pleased with you, O lord of kings; let a boon be accepted from me."

sanskrit: kuśika uvāca agnimadhyagatenedaṃ bhagavan saṃnidhau mayā vartitaṃ bhṛguśārdūla yan na dagdho 'smi tad bahu
english: Kuśika said: O blessed one, it was as one standing amid fire that I conducted myself in your presence, O tiger of the Bhṛgus; that I was not burned up—that is boon enough.

sanskrit: eṣa eva varo mukhyaḥ prāpto me bhṛgunandana yat prīto 'si samācārāt kulaṃ pūtaṃ mamānagha
english: This is the chief boon I have gained, O joy of the Bhṛgus: that you are pleased with my conduct, and my line is made pure, O sinless one.

sanskrit: eṣa me 'nugraho vipra jīvite ca prayojanam etad rājyaphalaṃ caiva tapaś caitat paraṃ mama
english: This is grace enough for me, O brāhmaṇa, and the very purpose of my life; this is the fruit of my kingship, and this my highest austerity.

sanskrit: yadi tu prītimān vipra mayi tvaṃ bhṛgunandana asti me saṃśayaḥ kaś cit tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: But if you are well pleased with me, O brāhmaṇa, joy of the Bhṛgus, there is a certain doubt in me; that you ought to explain to me.

sanskrit: cyavana uvāca varaś ca gṛhyatāṃ matto yaś ca te saṃśayo hṛdi taṃ ca brūhi naraśreṣṭha sarvaṃ saṃpādayāmi te
english: Cyavana said: Let a boon be taken from me; and whatever doubt is in your heart, declare it, O best of men—all of it I shall resolve for you.

sanskrit: kuśika uvāca yadi prīto 'si bhagavaṃs tato me vada bhārgava kāraṇaṃ śrotum icchāmi madgṛhe vāsakāritam
english: Kuśika said: If you are pleased, O blessed one, then tell me, O descendant of Bhṛgu—I wish to hear the reason for the dwelling you made in my house:

sanskrit: śayanaṃ caikapārśvena divasān ekaviṃśatim akiṃcid uktvā gamanaṃ bahiś ca munipuṃgava
english: your lying on one side for twenty-one days, your going outside without saying a word, O bull among sages,

sanskrit: antardhānam akasmāc ca punar eva ca darśanam punaś ca śayanaṃ vipra divasān ekaviṃśatim
english: your sudden disappearance and again your reappearance, and once more your lying down, O brāhmaṇa, for twenty-one days;

sanskrit: tailābhyaktasya gamanaṃ bhojanaṃ ca gṛhe mama samupānīya vividhaṃ yad dagdhaṃ jātavedasā niryāṇaṃ ca rathenāśu sahasā yat kṛtaṃ tvayā
english: your departure when anointed with oil, and your eating in my house; and how, when manifold food had been brought together, it was burned by Jātavedas the fire; and how you suddenly set out swiftly in the chariot;

sanskrit: dhanānāṃ ca visargasya vanasyāpi ca darśanam prāsādānāṃ bahūnāṃ ca kāñcanānāṃ mahāmune
english: and the squandering of my riches, and the apparition of the forest, and of the many golden palaces, O great sage,

sanskrit: maṇividrumapādānāṃ paryaṅkānāṃ ca darśanam punaś cādarśanaṃ tasya śrotum icchāmi kāraṇam
english: and the sight of couches with legs of gem and coral, and then again the vanishing of all that—I wish to hear the reason.

sanskrit: atīva hy atra muhyāmi cintayāno divāniśam na caivātrādhigacchāmi sarvasyāsya viniścayam etad icchāmi kārtsnyena satyaṃ śrotuṃ tapodhana
english: For in this I am utterly bewildered, brooding day and night, and I cannot arrive at any certainty about all of it; this I wish to hear in full and truly, O you whose wealth is austerity.

sanskrit: cyavana uvāca śṛṇu sarvam aśeṣeṇa yad idaṃ yena hetunā na hi śakyam anākhyātum evaṃ pṛṣṭena pārthiva
english: Cyavana said: Hear all of it without remainder—this thing, and the reason for it; for being so questioned, O king, I cannot leave it untold.

sanskrit: pitāmahasya vadataḥ purā devasamāgame śrutavān asmi yad rājaṃs tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: What I once heard the Grandsire say at an assembly of the gods, that, O king, hear from me as I relate it.

sanskrit: brahmakṣatravirodhena bhavitā kulasaṃkaraḥ pautras te bhavitā rājaṃs tejovīryasamanvitaḥ
english: "Through the strife of Brāhmaṇa and Kṣatriya there shall come a mingling of lines; a grandson shall be born to you, O king, endowed with brilliance and might.

sanskrit: tataḥ svakularakṣārtham ahaṃ tvā samupāgamam cikīrṣan kuśikocchedaṃ saṃdidhakṣuḥ kulaṃ tava
english: Therefore, to safeguard my own line, I came to you, O Kuśika, seeking to bring about your extinction, longing to burn up your house.

sanskrit: tato 'ham āgamya purā tvām avocaṃ mahīpate niyamaṃ kaṃ cid ārapsye śuśrūṣā kriyatām iti
english: So, having come to you then, O lord of the earth, I said: "I shall undertake a certain observance; let attendance be rendered to me."

sanskrit: na ca te duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃ cid aham āsādayaṃ gṛhe tena jīvasi rājarṣe na bhavethās tato 'nyathā
english: But I found no fault whatever in your house; by that you live, O royal sage—otherwise it would have been far otherwise with you.

sanskrit: etāṃ buddhiṃ samāsthāya divasān ekaviṃśatim supto 'smi yadi māṃ kaś cid bodhayed iti pārthiva
english: With this intent I slept for twenty-one days, thinking, "If anyone should wake me…," O king.

sanskrit: yadā tvayā sabhāryeṇa saṃsupto na prabodhitaḥ ahaṃ tadaiva te prīto manasā rājasattama
english: When neither you nor your wife roused me from sleep, at that very moment I was pleased with you in my heart, O best of kings.

sanskrit: utthāya cāsmi niṣkrānto yadi māṃ tvaṃ mahīpate pṛccheḥ kva yāsyasīty evaṃ śapeyaṃ tvām iti prabho
english: And I rose and went out, thinking, "If you, O lord of the earth, should ask me, 'Where are you going?'—then I would curse you," O lord.

sanskrit: antarhitaś cāsmi punaḥ punar eva ca te gṛhe yogam āsthāya saṃviṣṭo divasān ekaviṃśatim
english: And I made myself vanish, and again and again, in your house, taking up yoga, I lay down for twenty-one days.

sanskrit: kṣudhito mām asūyethāḥ śramād veti narādhipa etāṃ buddhiṃ samāsthāya karśitau vāṃ mayā kṣudhā
english: Thinking, "Perhaps, hungry or worn with toil, he will resent me," O lord of men—with this intent I wasted you both with hunger.

sanskrit: na ca te 'bhūt susūkṣmo 'pi manyur manasi pārthiva sabhāryasya naraśreṣṭha tena te prītimān aham
english: Yet not the slightest anger arose in your mind, O king, nor in your wife's, O best of men; therefore I am pleased with you.

sanskrit: bhojanaṃ ca samānāyya yat tad ādīpitaṃ mayā krudhyethā yadi mātsaryād iti tan marṣitaṃ ca te
english: And when I gathered the food and set it ablaze—thinking, "Perhaps out of resentment he will grow wrathful"—that too you endured.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ ratham āruhya tvām avocaṃ narādhipa sabhāryo māṃ vahasveti tac ca tvaṃ kṛtavāṃs tathā
english: Then I mounted the chariot and said to you, O lord of men, "Together with your wife, draw me along"—and that too you did.

sanskrit: aviśaṅko narapate prīto 'haṃ cāpi tena te dhanotsarge 'pi ca kṛte na tvāṃ krodhaḥ pradharṣayat
english: Without misgiving, O lord of men—and by that too I was pleased with you; even when the squandering of your wealth was done, no anger overcame you.

sanskrit: tataḥ prītena te rājan punar etat kṛtaṃ tava sabhāryasya vanaṃ bhūyas tad viddhi manujādhipa
english: Then, being pleased, O king, I did this once more for you and your wife—that forest; know it for what it was, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: prītyarthaṃ tava caitan me svargasaṃdarśanaṃ kṛtam yat te vane 'smin nṛpate dṛṣṭaṃ divyaṃ nidarśanam
english: And for your delight this showing of heaven was made by me—that divine vision which you beheld in this forest, O king.

sanskrit: svargoddeśas tvayā rājan saśarīreṇa pārthiva muhūrtam anubhūto 'sau sabhāryeṇa nṛpottama
english: That region of heaven, O king, you experienced in your own body for a moment, together with your wife, O best of kings.

sanskrit: nidarśanārthaṃ tapaso dharmasya ca narādhipa tatra yāsīt spṛhā rājaṃs tac cāpi viditaṃ mama
english: It was to give a glimpse of austerity and of dharma, O lord of men; the longing that arose in you there, O king, that too is known to me.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇyaṃ kāṅkṣase hi tvaṃ tapaś ca pṛthivīpate avamanya narendratvaṃ devendratvaṃ ca pārthiva
english: For you long for Brāhmaṇhood and for austerity, O lord of the earth, disdaining the rank of a king and even the rank of Indra of the gods, O monarch.

sanskrit: evam etad yathāttha tvaṃ brāhmaṇyaṃ tāta durlabham brāhmaṇye sati carṣitvam ṛṣitve ca tapasvitā
english: It is as you say, my son: Brāhmaṇhood is hard to attain; where there is Brāhmaṇhood there comes seerhood, and in seerhood the life of austerity.

sanskrit: bhaviṣyaty eṣa te kāmaḥ kuśikāt kauśiko dvijaḥ tṛtīyaṃ puruṣaṃ prāpya brāhmaṇatvaṃ gamiṣyati
english: This desire of yours shall be fulfilled: from Kuśika a Kauśika brāhmaṇa shall arise, who, reaching the third generation, shall attain Brāhmaṇhood.

sanskrit: vaṃśas te pārthivaśreṣṭha bhṛgūṇām eva tejasā pautras te bhavitā vipra tapasvī pāvakadyutiḥ
english: Your line, O best of kings, shall through the very brilliance of the Bhṛgus—your grandson shall become a brāhmaṇa, an ascetic, with the splendor of fire,

sanskrit: yaḥ sa devamanuṣyāṇāṃ bhayam utpādayiṣyati trayāṇāṃ caiva lokānāṃ satyam etad bravīmi te
english: who shall strike fear into gods and men and into the three worlds alike—this I tell you in truth.

sanskrit: varaṃ gṛhāṇa rājarṣe yas te manasi vartate tīrthayātrāṃ gamiṣyāmi purā kālo 'tivartate
english: Take the boon, O royal sage, that lies in your heart; I shall set out on a pilgrimage to the sacred fords, for the time slips by.

sanskrit: kuśika uvāca eṣa eva varo me 'dya yat tvaṃ prīto mahāmune bhavatv etad yathāttha tvaṃ tapaḥ pautre mamānagha brāhmaṇyaṃ me kulasyāstu bhagavann eṣa me varaḥ
english: Kuśika said: This is my very boon today—that you are pleased, O great sage. May it be as you have said: let there be austerity in my grandson, O sinless one, and Brāhmaṇhood for my line, O blessed one; this is the boon I ask.

sanskrit: punaś cākhyātum icchāmi bhagavan vistareṇa vai katham eṣyati vipratvaṃ kulaṃ me bhṛgunandana kaś cāsau bhavitā bandhur mama kaś cāpi saṃmataḥ
english: And again I wish you to explain in full, O blessed one: how shall my line come to brāhmaṇa-hood, O joy of the Bhṛgus? And who shall be that kinsman of mine, and who the one esteemed among them?

sanskrit: cyavana uvāca avaśyaṃ kathanīyaṃ me tavaitan narapuṃgava yadarthaṃ tvāham ucchettuṃ saṃprāpto manujādhipa
english: Cyavana said: This must surely be told to you, O bull among men—the very reason for which I came to destroy you, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: bhṛgūṇāṃ kṣatriyā yājyā nityam eva janādhipa te ca bhedaṃ gamiṣyanti daivayuktena hetunā
english: The Kṣatriyas are ever the patrons whose sacrifices the Bhṛgus perform, O lord of men; yet they shall fall into discord through a cause ordained by fate.

sanskrit: kṣatriyāś ca bhṛgūn sarvān vadhiṣyanti narādhipa ā garbhād anukṛntanto daivadaṇḍanipīḍitāḥ
english: And the Kṣatriyas shall slay all the Bhṛgus, O lord of men, cutting them down even to the embryo in the womb, driven by the rod of destiny.

sanskrit: tata utpatsyate 'smākaṃ kule gotravivardhanaḥ aurvo nāma mahātejā jvalanārkasamadyutiḥ
english: Then in our line shall be born one who shall increase the lineage, named Aurva, of great brilliance, with a radiance like blazing fire and sun.

sanskrit: sa trailokyavināśāya kopāgniṃ janayiṣyati mahīṃ saparvatavanāṃ yaḥ kariṣyati bhasmasāt
english: He shall give birth to a fire of wrath to destroy the three worlds—a fire that would reduce the earth, with its mountains and forests, to ashes.

sanskrit: kaṃ cit kālaṃ tu taṃ vahniṃ sa eva śamayiṣyati samudre vaḍavāvaktre prakṣipya munisattamaḥ
english: But after some time that best of sages shall himself quell that fire, casting it into the ocean within the mare's mouth.

sanskrit: putraṃ tasya mahābhāgam ṛcīkaṃ bhṛgunandanam sākṣāt kṛtsno dhanurvedaḥ samupasthāsyate 'nagha
english: Upon his illustrious son Ṛcīka, joy of the Bhṛgus, the whole science of archery shall present itself in visible form, O sinless one,

sanskrit: kṣatriyāṇām abhāvāya daivayuktena hetunā sa tu taṃ pratigṛhyaiva putre saṃkrāmayiṣyati
english: for the undoing of the Kṣatriyas, through a cause ordained by fate; and he, having received it, shall pass it on to his son.

sanskrit: jamadagnau mahābhāge tapasā bhāvitātmani sa cāpi bhṛguśārdūlas taṃ vedaṃ dhārayiṣyati
english: To Jamadagni, the illustrious, his soul refined by austerity; and that tiger of the Bhṛgus too shall hold that science.

sanskrit: kulāt tu tava dharmātman kanyāṃ so 'dhigamiṣyati udbhāvanārthaṃ bhavato vaṃśasya nṛpasattama
english: And from your line, O righteous one, he shall obtain a maiden, for the raising up of your house, O best of kings.

sanskrit: gādher duhitaraṃ prāpya pautrīṃ tava mahātapāḥ brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatradharmāṇaṃ rāmam utpādayiṣyati
english: Gaining the daughter of Gādhi, your granddaughter, that great ascetic shall beget Rāma, a brāhmaṇa with the ways of a Kṣatriya.

sanskrit: kṣatriyaṃ viprakarmāṇaṃ bṛhaspatim ivaujasā viśvāmitraṃ tava kule gādheḥ putraṃ sudhārmikam tapasā mahatā yuktaṃ pradāsyati mahādyute
english: And in your line he shall bring forth Viśvāmitra, son of Gādhi—a Kṣatriya with the works of a brāhmaṇa, in might like Bṛhaspati, deeply righteous, endowed with great austerity, O you of great splendor.

sanskrit: striyau tu kāraṇaṃ tatra parivarte bhaviṣyataḥ pitāmahaniyogād vai nānyathaitad bhaviṣyati
english: Two women shall be the cause of this exchange; by the ordinance of the Grandsire it shall not be otherwise.

sanskrit: tṛtīye puruṣe tubhyaṃ brāhmaṇatvam upaiṣyati bhavitā tvaṃ ca saṃbandhī bhṛgūṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām
english: In the third generation Brāhmaṇhood shall come to you, and you shall become a kinsman of the Bhṛgus, whose souls are refined.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca kuśikas tu muner vākyaṃ cyavanasya mahātmanaḥ śrutvā hṛṣṭo 'bhavad rājā vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha evam astv iti dharmātmā tadā bharatasattama
english: Bhīṣma said: When king Kuśika heard the words of the great-souled sage Cyavana, he was filled with joy, and that righteous one spoke this word: "So be it," O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: cyavanas tu mahātejāḥ punar eva narādhipam varārthaṃ codayām āsa tam uvāca sa pārthivaḥ
english: But Cyavana of great brilliance again urged the lord of men to take a boon; and the king said to him:

sanskrit: bāḍham evaṃ grahīṣyāmi kāmaṃ tvatto mahāmune brahmabhūtaṃ kulaṃ me 'stu dharme cāsya mano bhavet
english: "Surely, even so I shall gladly accept it from you, O great sage: let my line become brahman-like, and let its mind be set upon dharma."

sanskrit: evam uktas tathety evaṃ pratyuktvā cyavano muniḥ abhyanujñāya nṛpatiṃ tīrthayātrāṃ yayau tadā
english: Thus addressed, the sage Cyavana answered, "So be it," and, taking leave of the king, then set out upon his pilgrimage to the sacred fords.

sanskrit: etat te kathitaṃ sarvam aśeṣeṇa mayā nṛpa bhṛgūṇāṃ kuśikānāṃ ca prati saṃbandhakāraṇam
english: All this I have told you without remainder, O king—the cause of the kinship between the Bhṛgus and the Kuśikas.

sanskrit: yathoktaṃ muninā cāpi tathā tad abhavan nṛpa janma rāmasya ca muner viśvāmitrasya caiva ha
english: And just as it was foretold by the sage, so it came to pass, O king—the birth of the sage Rāma and of Viśvāmitra as well.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca muhyāmīva niśamyādya cintayānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ hīnāṃ pārthivasaṃghātaiḥ śrīmadbhiḥ pṛthivīm imām
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I seem to swoon today as I hear, brooding again and again over this earth bereft of its bands of glorious kings.

sanskrit: prāpya rājyāni śataśo mahīṃ jitvāpi bhārata koṭiśaḥ puruṣān hatvā paritapye pitāmaha
english: Having gained kingdoms by the hundred and conquered the earth, O Bhārata, having slain men by the tens of millions, I am consumed with anguish, O grandfather.

sanskrit: kā nu tāsāṃ varastrīṇām avasthādya bhaviṣyati yā hīnāḥ patibhiḥ putrair mātulair bhrātṛbhis tathā
english: What shall now be the lot of those noble women who are bereft of husbands, of sons, of maternal uncles, and of brothers?

sanskrit: vayaṃ hi tān gurūn hatvā jñātīṃś ca suhṛdo 'pi ca avākśīrṣāḥ patiṣyāmo narake nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: For we, having slain our elders and kinsmen and friends as well, shall surely fall headlong into hell; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: śarīraṃ yoktum icchāmi tapasogreṇa bhārata upadiṣṭam ihecchāmi tattvato 'haṃ viśāṃ pate
english: I wish to yoke this body to fierce austerity, O Bhārata; I wish to be instructed herein according to the truth, O lord of men.
